claims.value: Recovered prior causal state: about 196 GiB was retained in legacy session tables. Earlier sampling showed writes flowing to compact replacement tables rather than legacy counterparts. The new six-hour observation measured 68 GiB of filesystem free space, stable within 1 GiB; legacy session tables remained at zero writes per second while compact replacement tables continued receiving active writes. answer.answer: Revised child checkpoint: use three occupied level-0 Base Cores, dedicating one core to each heavy machine. No two requested machines may share a core. Construction remains gated on confirming that existing and supporting heat keeps each core at or below 1,000.

claims.value: The prior durable architecture was an Update 1-only distributed backbone-and-spurs factory with protected core hubs, modular production cells, mining spurs, single-item rail lines and buffers, and rail upgrades driven by measured throughput rather than a monolithic mega-base.

The new requirement is one Constructorizer and two Facturers while every Base Core remains level 0. Their machine heat is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800 total. A level-0 core has 1,000 capacity, and exceeding it disables Fire Wave protection.

The safe revised layout uses at least three occupied level-0 cores: Core A hosts only the Constructorizer at 500 heat, leaving 500 capacity; Core B hosts only Facturer 1 at 650 heat, leaving 350; Core C hosts only Facturer 2 at 650 heat, leaving 350. Constructorizer plus Facturer is unsafe at 1,150, two Facturers are unsafe at 1,300, and all three are unsafe at 1,800, so every requested heavy machine must be isolated from the others. Existing and support-building heat must fit inside the stated remaining capacity at its respective core.

Before construction, inspect each intended core's live load and Update 1 unlocks, budget all required support heat, and proceed only where the projected total is no more than 1,000. Use only confirmed Update 1 equipment; do not rely on hidden or future content, disputed amplifier values, or pre-Update-1 guidance.

decisions: Reject every heavy-machine co-location: Constructorizer plus Facturer totals 1,150; two Facturers total 1,300; all three total 1,800. Each exceeds the 1,000 level-0 limit.
Use a minimum of three occupied level-0 cores: Core A for the Constructorizer only, Core B for Facturer 1 only, and Core C for Facturer 2 only.
Treat each core's remaining 500/350/350 capacity as a hard envelope for all existing load, power generation, extraction, processing, storage, and other heat-bearing support assigned to that core.
Preserve the distributed rail backbone, but use only confirmed Update 1 rail tiers and equipment. Do not depend on Rail v.4/v.5, hidden buildings, future recipes, or unverified amplifier cooling.
Do not begin construction until live core loads plus the complete planned support load have been measured and shown to remain at or below 1,000 on every occupied core.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge and live resumable work state so later agents can inspect, revise, advance, and hand off complex work with source fidelity.

claims.value: The recovered parent architecture is an Update 1-only distributed backbone-and-spurs factory using modular production cells, powered rails, single-item buffers, and measured-throughput rail upgrades; the monolithic mega-base is superseded.

The revised requirement is one Constructorizer plus two Facturers while all Base Cores remain level 0. Their machine heat is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800; Constructorizer+Facturer is 1,150 and Facturer+Facturer is 1,300, so every two-machine co-location exceeds a level-0 core's 1,000 capacity and would disable Fire Wave protection.

The safe revised layout uses three distinct occupied level-0 cores: Core A hosts only the Constructorizer at 500 heat, while Cores B and C each host one Facturer at 650 heat. Raw remaining capacities are 500, 350, and 350 respectively, and all auxiliary powered loads must fit within those limits.

Before building, inspect each live Core panel and Update 1 build menu, include every auxiliary powered structure in projected load, and proceed only when each occupied core remains at or below 1,000 without disputed amplifier credit. Use only visible, currently unlocked Update 1 equipment and upgrade rail tiers only when measured throughput requires it.

claims.value: Straylight is an agent-first portable context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge together with live, resumable work state.

The 17/20 workspace result did not demonstrate superiority, but its token total is not directly comparable with one-shot top-k until cumulative cached replay and uncached input are reported separately; it is not an architecture verdict.

The first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned workspace implementing typed resume, N→N+1 refresh/diff, batched query/read with exact and lexical retrieval plus an injectable semantic path, and immutable parent-linked checkpoint commit with source references.

The transition passes when a fixture reopens a revision-N parent, exposes known N→N+1 evidence without full-corpus reconstruction, matches direct-filesystem claims, commits a source-preserving child, completes within four workspace calls, and separately reports cached replay and uncached input.
